title: Picking up stitches along a horizontal edge
subtitle: Adding live stitches from a cast-on or cast-off edge for borders and neckbands.
excerpt: Picking up stitches along a horizontal edge draws new loops through the cast-on or cast-off row so a border, neckband, or button band can be worked upward. The rate is usually one stitch for every existing stitch along the edge.
sourceNotes: Standard technique documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938) and Weldon's Practical Knitter garment finishing notes. Pick-up rates for horizontal edges are described in UK pattern writing convention.
heroPrompt: A knitting needle picking up loops through the cast-off edge of a neckline, stitches forming a tidy row ready to work downward.

glossaryTerms.definition: To insert the needle through an existing edge of the fabric and draw a new loop of yarn through it, creating a live stitch ready to be worked in the next row.

content.text: along a horizontal edge draws new stitches from the cast-on or cast-off row. The edge runs parallel to the needle, and each existing stitch has a clearly defined loop to pick up through. This contrasts with picking up along a vertical edge, where the row gauge (taller than the stitch gauge) means you must skip some rows. Along a horizontal edge, the pick-up is usually one stitch for every stitch on the edge. Difficulty: beginner.
The finished knitted piece with the cast-on or cast-off edge ready
A knitting needle in the correct diameter for the border or neckband
Working yarn attached or a new length ready to join
Hold the piece with the right side facing you and the edge along which you are picking up running horizontally in front of you.
Join the yarn at the right-hand end of the edge. Insert the needle tip under both legs of the first stitch on the edge (or under the corresponding V of the cast-on chain).
Wrap the yarn around the needle as if to knit and draw a new loop through to the front. One stitch picked up.
Move along the edge and repeat, picking up one stitch from each existing stitch. Along a cast-off edge, the pick-up ratio is 1:1; along a cast-on edge, it is also usually 1:1.
If the pattern calls for fewer stitches than the edge has, space the reductions evenly. Skip every nth edge stitch as the pattern instructs.

Picking up along a horizontal edge is used for straight neckbands, button bands on cardigan fronts, and sock cuffs on toe-up socks. The same technique applies wherever a cast-on or cast-off edge needs to grow a new section of fabric.

items.symptom: The picked-up edge ripples or flutes outward
items.cause: Too many stitches picked up relative to the number of rows in the border stitch
items.fix: Reduce the stitch count. If the pattern gives a precise count, trust it over the 1:1 rate. Alternatively, decrease evenly on the first row of the border.

items.cause: Too few stitches picked up, or the yarn was pulled too tight during pick-up
items.fix: Increase the stitch count or pick up more loosely. The border should lie flat against the main fabric without pulling.

items.symptom: Holes appear along the picked-up edge
items.cause: The needle went through only one leg of the stitch rather than under both
items.fix: Insert the needle cleanly under both legs of the V at the top of each stitch on the cast-off edge.
